title: Forward Deployed Engineering at Cursor — Pauline Brunet
talk_summary: Pauline Brunet describes Cursor's Forward Deployed Engineering function: how to decide when FDE is appropriate (customer digital maturity × product customization matrix), how to hire and structure the team, and how to scope engagements around measurable ROI.

takeaways.technique: Directional scoping with explicit success criteria and phased delivery
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of open-ended staffing ('two FTEs for six months'), they scope a specific problem, define what success looks like up front, and commit only to directional phases (e.g. phase one and two over six weeks) so they can pivot as they learn.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you cannot just do like, 'Hey, take two FTEs for 6 months, do whatever you want with them.' I think that's a recipe for failure

takeaways.technique: Define success before starting, with a baseline number
takeaways.what_they_do: They force the customer to state a measurable baseline and target ('3 hours to 20 minutes') and confirm that hitting it counts as success before work begins.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If I automate this process from start to finish and then now takes 20 minutes instead of 3 hours, which is current baseline, is that sufficient for you?

takeaways.technique: ROI framing: revenue, cost, or risk
takeaways.what_they_do: Every engagement is justified as increasing revenue, decreasing cost, or mitigating risk, and that ROI is over-communicated rather than left implicit.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's always three things, super simple. Am I increasing revenue? Am I decreasing costs? Or am I mitigating risks?

takeaways.technique: Say no to out-of-scope work to protect credibility
takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly decline use cases where the product isn't the right tool, both to build trust and to avoid being on the hook for failures.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I have customers who'll say, 'I want to do this.' And I will say, 'Ooh, Cursor is not the right tool for that.'

takeaways.what_they_do: At the end of an engagement they hand over documentation so the customer can sustain the work without them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: leave your documentation artifacts behind so that you can help them
